_metadata.title: High-Speed Interface Wiring Research for D38999 Connector Selection
_metadata.purpose: Reference data for the D38999 agent to determine contact types, pin groupings, and feasibility when routing high-speed interfaces through MIL-DTL-38999 connectors

sources.title: USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification Release 2.4
RGB Parallel Display Interface (DPI)
sources.organization: Various SoC vendors (Raspberry Pi, STM32, NXP i.MX)

interface_comparison.typical_use: Universal connector system (data + power + alt modes)

usb2.name: USB 2.0

pair_groups.notes: Must be adjacent in connector. Keep as twisted pair.

d38999_guidance.conditions: Short cable (<2m), validated assembly, or low-speed only (Full Speed 12 Mbps). For High Speed 480 Mbps through D38999, controlled routing and SI validation are required.
layout_rules: Place D+ and D- in adjacent cavities
Keep GND contact adjacent to D+/D- pair
VBUS on separate contact, adequately sized for current
Shell bond for shield continuity
Do not share USB GND with high-current noisy power return
d38999_guidance.preferred_solution: Twinax contact for D+/D- pair if High Speed (480 Mbps) is required

usb2.spare_pin_policy: 1-2 spares for future expansion (e.g., OTG ID pin)
warnings: USB 2.0 High Speed (480 Mbps) requires 90Ω differential impedance on D+/D-
Eye diagram validation recommended for production High Speed designs
Cable shield must terminate to connector shell for EMC compliance
Do not split D+ and D- across unrelated connector regions
ESD protection recommended at both ends

usb3.name: USB 3.x SuperSpeed

pair_groups.notes: SuperSpeed TX pair. Must be shielded and controlled impedance.
SuperSpeed RX pair. Must be shielded and controlled impedance.

d38999_guidance.contact_type: Twinax or Quadrax contacts required for SuperSpeed pairs
d38999_guidance.conditions: Generic signal contacts are NOT acceptable for reliable USB 3.x operation. The entire interconnect (contacts + cable + termination) must be validated for 5+ Gbps signal integrity.
layout_rules: Use Twinax contacts for USB3_TX pair
Use Twinax contacts for USB3_RX pair
USB2 D+/D- can use normal contacts (or separate Twinax)
Keep SuperSpeed pairs physically separated from high-current power
Preserve shield continuity through connector
Minimize stub lengths
TX and RX direction depends on host/device role
d38999_guidance.preferred_solution: Purpose-built USB 3.x rated D38999 insert or qualified high-speed cable assembly

usb3.spare_pin_policy: 1-2 signal spares for debug/test; no spare on high-speed pairs
warnings: Generic D38999 signal contacts are usually NOT appropriate for USB 3.x
Signal integrity validation (eye diagram, insertion loss, return loss) is mandatory
SuperSpeed uses separate TX and RX pairs — direction depends on host/device role
TX/RX crossing may be needed depending on connector role
Cable length limited to ~3m for passive copper at 5 Gbps
Common-mode chokes and ESD protection may be needed at board level
Do not route SuperSpeed pairs near high-current switching power contacts

usb_type_c.name: USB Type-C
usb_type_c.standard: USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification (USB-IF)
usb_type_c.description: USB Type-C is a connector SYSTEM, not just a pinout. It includes orientation detection, power delivery negotiation, and alternate mode support.

signals_24pin.name: CC1
signals_24pin.description: Configuration Channel 1 — orientation, current advertisement, PD comms

signals_24pin.name: CC2
signals_24pin.description: Configuration Channel 2 — orientation, VCONN for active cables

usb2_only.notes: Requires CC resistors (5.1kΩ pull-down for sink, Rp for source) at each end. No mux needed.

usb3_single_lane.notes: Requires orientation mux or fixed orientation. CC controller needed. Twinax contacts for SS pairs.

usb_pd_power_only.description: USB-C Power Delivery (charging only, no data)
usb_pd_power_only.notes: Requires USB PD controller IC at each end. VBUS voltage negotiated (5V-48V). Current up to 5A. E-marker for >3A or >60W.

dp_alt_mode.notes: Uses 2 or 4 SuperSpeed lanes for DP. Requires USB-C/PD controller + DP Alt Mode logic. NOT a simple pin-mapping exercise.

usb4_thunderbolt.notes: DO NOT attempt through generic D38999. Requires full USB4 PHY, retimers, extremely demanding SI.

d38999_guidance.critical_warning: Do NOT tell the user to 'just wire USB-C pins through D38999'. USB-C requires active electronics (CC controller, orientation mux, PD controller) at each end.
decision_tree: 1. Determine which USB-C FUNCTION is needed (USB2? USB3? Power? Alt Mode?)
2. For USB 2.0 only: Extract D+/D- + VBUS/GND + CC resistors → feasible with normal contacts
3. For USB 3.x: Extract SS pairs + USB2 + CC → requires Twinax contacts + controller board
4. For USB PD power: Extract VBUS/GND + CC → requires PD controller at each end
5. For Alt Mode / USB4: Recommend board-level USB-C connector at each end, linked by appropriate D38999 cable for the underlying signal (DP lanes, etc.)

usb_type_c.spare_pin_policy: 2-3 spares; reserve for SBU signals if Alt Mode may be added later
warnings: USB-C is NOT just a connector pinout — it is a full configuration/negotiation system
CC pins MUST have proper resistors or a CC/PD controller at each end
Orientation detection requires either a mux or fixed wiring (losing reversibility)
Power Delivery requires a PD controller IC for voltage/current negotiation
E-marker cable electronics required for >60W or >5 Gbps cables
High-power USB-C (>60W) involves voltage up to 48V — safety and thermal design required
Do NOT blindly extend all 24 Type-C pins through D38999 without professional design
For Alt Mode, the underlying video interface (DP, HDMI) determines the contact requirements

hdmi.name: HDMI

signals.name: HDMI_CLK_P
signals.description: TMDS/FRL Clock+ (4th data channel in HDMI 2.1+)

signals.name: HDMI_CEC
signals.description: Consumer Electronics Control (one-wire bidirectional serial bus)

signals.name: HDMI_HPD
signals.description: Hot Plug Detect / ARC- / HEC- / eARC-

cec.description: Single-wire Consumer Electronics Control bus referenced to HDMI ground.
notes: Low-speed control channel; normal signal contacts are acceptable.
Keep CEC away from TMDS/FRL pairs and noisy power conductors.

ddc.description: EDID / HDCP management channel implemented as I2C plus a low-current +5V supply.
notes: Group SCL, SDA, and ground together; +5V remains low current but is required for hot-plug and EDID behavior.
Normal signal contacts are acceptable for DDC and +5V when the TMDS/FRL pairs use qualified high-speed contacts.

arc_hec_earc_bundle.description: Shared auxiliary conductor set used for ARC, HEC, and eARC features depending on HDMI version and equipment implementation.

arc.purpose: Audio Return Channel from sink back to source
notes: Uses the utility / HPD conductor group centered on pins 14 and 19 with pin 17 as the associated ground/reference.
Do not repurpose HDMI_UTILITY if audio return may be required later.

hec.purpose: HDMI Ethernet Channel over the shared HEAC conductors
notes: Also uses the same pin 14 / pin 19 conductor group with pin 17 reference.
Rare in deployed products; validate endpoint support before allocating contacts for HEC.

earc.purpose: Enhanced Audio Return Channel with higher-performance discovery and audio transport requirements
notes: Reuses the same utility / HPD conductor group with tighter implementation requirements than legacy ARC.
Preserve pin 14, pin 19, and nearby ground continuity through the ruggedized transition if eARC compatibility matters.

d38999_guidance.contact_type: Twinax or Quadrax contacts required for all 4 TMDS/FRL pairs
d38999_guidance.low_speed_contacts: Normal signal contacts acceptable for DDC_SDA, DDC_SCL, CEC, HDMI_UTILITY, HPD, and +5V
layout_rules: Each TMDS/FRL pair in its own Twinax or Quadrax contact cavity
Keep per-pair shields/returns
DDC (I2C) SDA/SCL grouped together with ground nearby
CEC separate from high-speed pairs
If ARC, HEC, or eARC is required, reserve the HDMI_UTILITY / HDMI_HPD conductor group and keep HDMI_GND nearby as its reference/return
HPD and +5V separate from TMDS
+5V current is low (50mA max) — #22D contact sufficient
Shell/shield continuity for EMC

feasibility_by_version.hdmi_1.x_1080p: Possible with Twinax contacts and validated cable assembly
feasibility_by_version.hdmi_2.0_4k60: Difficult — requires Premium High Speed cable equivalent. Twinax/Quadrax + SI validation.
feasibility_by_version.hdmi_2.1_4k120_8k: Extremely difficult. Ultra High Speed cable. Avoid unless purpose-built solution.

total_d38999_contacts_needed.low_speed_signal: 5 normal contacts (CEC, DDC_SDA, DDC_SCL, HPD, UTILITY/ARC)

warnings: HDMI is high-speed and impedance-sensitive — DO NOT route through random contacts
DDC is I2C-like but full HDMI is NOT 'just I2C + video'
HPD and +5V are essential for source/sink detection — cannot be omitted
Pins 14 and 19 are part of the optional ARC / HEC / eARC conductor set — do not treat HDMI_UTILITY as a generic spare signal if those features may be needed
HDMI 2.1 FRL is much more demanding than TMDS — may not be achievable through D38999
Signal integrity validation (eye diagram) required for any production implementation
If user only needs rugged video, consider DisplayPort, HD-SDI, or Ethernet video instead
Verify source vs sink direction and mating face orientation before pinout assignment

displayport.name: DisplayPort

signals.name: DP_AUX_P
signals.description: AUX Channel+ (1 Mbps sideband, Manchester encoded)

d38999_guidance.contact_type: Twinax contacts for each Main Link lane pair. Normal contacts for AUX, HPD, DP_PWR.
layout_rules: Each Main Link lane pair in Twinax contact
AUX channel pair in adjacent contacts (or Twinax if available)
HPD separate from high-speed lanes
DP_PWR (+3.3V) on adequately sized contact — do not source power incorrectly
Keep ground/shield contacts near each lane pair
Verify source vs sink orientation
d38999_guidance.lane_reduction: If bandwidth allows, 2-lane DP (HBR2/HBR3) may suffice for 1080p/1440p, reducing contact count

feasibility_by_version.dp_1.2_hbr2: Achievable with Twinax contacts and qualified cable assembly
feasibility_by_version.dp_1.4_hbr3: Difficult — higher insertion loss budget. Requires SI validation.

total_d38999_contacts_needed.4_lane: 4 Twinax (lanes) + 1 Twinax or 2 signal (AUX) + HPD + DP_PWR + GND = ~14 contacts
total_d38999_contacts_needed.2_lane_reduced: 2 Twinax (lanes) + AUX + HPD + DP_PWR + GND = ~10 contacts

warnings: DisplayPort main link is high-speed differential — requires controlled-impedance contacts
Generic D38999 contacts are NOT validated for DP data rates
AUX channel is lower speed but still differential — keep pair together
DP_PWR is source-to-sink — do NOT short between devices or source power backwards
USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode is different from native DP connector wiring
Lane count can be reduced (4→2→1) if resolution/refresh allows, saving contacts
Signal integrity validation required for production
For very long runs, consider fiber optic DP extender rather than copper through D38999

dvi.name: DVI (Digital Visual Interface)
dvi.standard: DVI Specification 1.0 (DDWG: Intel, Silicon Image, Compaq, Fujitsu, HP, IBM, NEC)

dvi_d_single.contact_type: 4x Twinax for TMDS pairs + normal contacts for DDC/HPD/+5V
dvi_d_single.notes: Same TMDS as HDMI 1.x. Validated cable assembly required.

dvi_d_dual.contact_type: 7x Twinax pairs = very large insert. Purpose-built solution preferred.
dvi_d_dual.notes: 7 high-speed differential pairs. Consider HDMI or DP conversion instead.

dvi_i.notes: Combines digital TMDS + analog video. Very complex. Consider separating digital and analog.

dvi_a.contact_type: 3x Coax for RGB + normal contacts for sync/DDC
dvi_a.notes: Treat like VGA. Coax contacts for RGB, signal contacts for sync/control.

warnings: Verify DVI variant (D/I/A) and link count (single/dual) FIRST
DVI-D digital TMDS pairs require controlled impedance (100Ω) — same as HDMI
DVI-I requires BOTH digital high-speed pairs AND analog coax — very complex
DVI dual-link needs 7 differential pairs — very large connector footprint
For DVI-D single-link, consider HDMI-to-D38999 approach (electrically compatible)
DDC pullups and +5V current must be verified
Generic D38999 signal contacts NOT recommended for TMDS

vga.name: VGA (Video Graphics Array / DE-15)

d38999_guidance.contact_type: Coax contacts for R/G/B video lines; normal signal contacts for sync and DDC
layout_rules: Use coax contacts (size 12 Coax) for VGA_R, VGA_G, VGA_B — each with own return
Keep each RGB color with its own return/shield (coax provides this inherently)
HSYNC and VSYNC on normal signal contacts, near ground
DDC SDA/SCL grouped with ground nearby
+5V on separate contact
Keep sync and DDC signals away from high-current switching power
d38999_guidance.generic_contact_alternative: For low resolution (≤800x600) or short cables (<1m), normal contacts may work with dedicated returns. Quality will be degraded.

total_d38999_contacts_needed.with_coax: 3 Coax (RGB) + 2 signal (H/V sync) + 2 signal (DDC) + 1 power (+5V) + 2 ground = 10 contacts
total_d38999_contacts_needed.without_coax: 3 signal (RGB) + 3 ground (returns) + 2 sync + 2 DDC + 1 power + 1 ground = 12 contacts

vga.spare_pin_policy: 1-2 spares; consider ID bits for monitor detection
warnings: VGA is ANALOG — signal quality depends on shielding, impedance, return paths, crosstalk
RGB lines should be treated like analog coax, not random logic wires
Poor wiring causes ghosting, blur, color shift, and noise
Each RGB signal needs its own individual return — do NOT share a single ground return
For high resolutions (>1080p equivalent), coax contacts are strongly recommended
DDC is I2C (for EDID) — keep SDA/SCL together with ground
VGA is legacy; consider converting to HDMI/DP digitally before the connector if possible

dpi_parallel_rgb.name: DPI / Parallel RGB
dpi_parallel_rgb.standard: Various SoC-specific (Raspberry Pi DPI, STM32 LTDC, i.MX eLCDIF, MIPI DPI)
dpi_parallel_rgb.description: Parallel display interface with individual data lines per color bit. NOT to be confused with MIPI DSI (serial).
dpi_parallel_rgb.note: DPI is primarily a board-level interface. Routing through a connector/cable is unusual and risky.

rgb565.signals: R[4:0], G[5:0], B[4:0] + PCLK + HSYNC + VSYNC + DE

rgb666.signals: R[5:0], G[5:0], B[5:0] + PCLK + HSYNC + VSYNC + DE

rgb888.signals: R[7:0], G[7:0], B[7:0] + PCLK + HSYNC + VSYNC + DE

d38999_guidance.primary_recommendation: Convert DPI to a serialized interface (LVDS, eDP, HDMI, or DSI) BEFORE crossing a rugged D38999 connector. DPI is a board-level interface not designed for cable/connector runs.

if_dpi_must_be_used.contact_type: Normal signal contacts with aggressive ground interleaving
layout_rules: Interleave ground pins: at least 1 GND per 4-6 data pins
Keep PCLK near ground contacts (critical reference)
Group RGB bits by color byte (R[7:0] together, G[7:0] together, B[7:0] together)
Keep HSYNC/VSYNC/DE near PCLK and ground
Match wire lengths within ±10mm for all data lines relative to PCLK
Use shielded cable
Reduce pixel clock speed if possible (use lower resolution)

serialization_alternatives.benefits: Reduces to 4-5 diff pairs, proven for display cables

serialization_alternatives.chips: TI SN65DSI86 (DSI to eDP) or parallel RGB to eDP

serialization_alternatives.benefits: Standard HDMI cable, widely available rugged connectors
Fewer wires, common in embedded displays

dpi_parallel_rgb.spare_pin_policy: 2-4 spares if using direct DPI; group with grounds
warnings: DPI/parallel RGB is NOT designed for cable runs — it is a board-level interface
Cable length, skew, EMI, and crosstalk are major problems
PCLK is the critical timing reference — all data must arrive within setup/hold window relative to PCLK
Long cables cause timing violations, color artifacts, and EMC failures
Strongly recommend serializing (LVDS/eDP/HDMI) before crossing any connector
If DPI must be used: keep cable <30cm, pixel clock <25 MHz, use shielded ribbon
Ground interleaving is mandatory — never route 24 data wires without ground returns
Do NOT confuse DPI (parallel RGB) with MIPI DSI (serial) — completely different interfaces

d38999_design_rules.condition: interface includes USB 3.x, HDMI, DisplayPort, or DVI-D
d38999_design_rules.details: Use Twinax, Quadrax, or manufacturer-specific high-speed contacts validated for the target data rate

d38999_design_rules.condition: interface is VGA and video quality matters
d38999_design_rules.details: Use size 12 Coax contacts for RGB analog video lines with individual returns

d38999_design_rules.condition: interface is DPI/parallel RGB and cable length > 30cm
d38999_design_rules.details: Convert to LVDS, eDP, or HDMI before the connector. DPI is not a cable interface.

d38999_design_rules.condition: interface is USB Type-C PD or Alt Mode
d38999_design_rules.details: USB-C requires CC controller, orientation logic, and PD negotiation. Do not directly map Type-C pins through D38999 without active electronics.
P and N of each differential pair MUST be in adjacent connector cavities. Never split a pair across the insert.
Each high-speed pair needs a dedicated shield/return. Use per-pair shielded contacts or ensure ground contacts adjacent to each pair.

d38999_design_rules.condition: high-speed pairs AND high-current power in same connector
d38999_design_rules.details: Keep high-current power contacts physically separated from high-speed differential pairs. Power switching noise couples into adjacent high-speed lines.
Document source (transmitter) vs sink (receiver) direction. Verify mating face orientation and mirror direction before finalizing pinout.

d38999_design_rules.condition: interface is HDMI 2.1 FRL, DP 2.0 UHBR, or USB4/Thunderbolt
d38999_design_rules.details: These interfaces exceed what typical D38999 contact geometries can support. Recommend purpose-built ruggedized video connectors or fiber optic solutions.

d38999_design_rules.condition: any interface with hot-plug detect (HPD) pin
d38999_design_rules.details: HPD is essential for source/sink detection. Cannot be omitted. Route as normal signal contact, not near high-speed pairs.
DDC SDA and SCL should be adjacent with ground nearby. Normal signal contacts are fine. Keep away from noisy power.
Signal integrity testing (eye diagram, insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk) is MANDATORY before production. D38999 contact geometry alone does not guarantee performance.

final_warnings: Final wiring must be verified against the exact standard revision in use
High-speed interfaces require controlled impedance, short discontinuities, correct shielding, and SI validation
D38999 insert geometry alone is NOT enough — contact technology and cable assembly design matter
Do NOT use generic signal contacts for USB 3.x, HDMI, DisplayPort, or DVI-D digital unless tested and validated
Official connector pin orientation (mating face vs wire side) and mirror direction must be verified before wiring
The D38999 connector shell provides overall shielding but individual pair shielding requires appropriate contact types
For HDMI 2.1, DP 2.0, USB4, or Thunderbolt — recommend purpose-built ruggedized solutions rather than generic D38999
When mixing high-speed video with power in the same connector, thermal and EMC testing is essential
